violations.why: Timer_C (higher priority) can preempt Timer_A between the read and the write-back of timerCount+1, so its update is lost.
Timer_Force (equal priority) can preempt Timer_A between the read and the write, so its update is lost.
Timer_C can overwrite timerCount after Timer_A stores it and before Timer_A tests it.
Timer_Force can overwrite timerCount after Timer_A stores it and before Timer_A tests it, so the test sees a different value.
Timer_C can change timerCount between Timer_A's read and its later check.
Timer_Force can change timerCount between Timer_A's read and its later check.
Timer_A (higher priority) can preempt Timer_B between its write of 0 and its check, so the check no longer sees 0.
Timer_C writes timerCount between Timer_B's write and its check; the value is 0 in this case, but the check is still not atomic with the write.
Timer_Force can set timerCount to 1 between Timer_B's write of 0 and its check.
